note: Three public-series briefs for a live run (an ordinary account on the deployment). Supply only the inputs; fixtures/reference_top_table.tsv, fixtures/source-manifest.json and reference_gse5583.R stay with the evaluator. The public data resource is the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, not the pharma GEO module. Offline reference agreement (runtime/mcp/evimed-research/test/test_gene_expression.py) is not live capability acceptance.

briefs.title: HDAC1 knock-out versus wild-type mouse embryonic stem cells (GSE5583)
briefs.why: A classic three-against-three Affymetrix series whose MAS5 values are linear, so the unit identity has to be judged before any statistic; the platform states no genome build; some probes map to several genes; and small groups are exactly where a Welch test is not limma.

inputs.groupDefinition: Compare the HDAC1 knock-out arrays with the wild-type arrays (knock-out minus wild type) and tell me which genes change most.

mustDo: Preserve the series with gene_expression_series and read its identity checks: one platform (GPL81), samples agreeing, genome build unknown (not assumed), values linear so log2 is applied and said.
Declare the two groups of three from the Genotype annotation, state the declaration, and compute with gene_expression_differential into a new directory under deliverables/.
Write the report with every number as a rendered reference through research_calculate action=render, and paste the tool's top table unchanged.

State that the method is a Welch test with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment and not limma, what that means with three arrays per group, that a probe mapped to several genes is one flagged row, and the series' stated dates.
mustNotDo: Compute or type any statistic, fold change or p value by hand.
Call the result a limma analysis, a pathway finding or evidence of a mechanism or treatment effect.
Assume a genome build, pool another platform, or choose the groups from the p values.
briefs.gradedOn: Agreement of the delivered top table with fixtures/reference_top_table.tsv (base R t.test and p.adjust(BH), computed from the same file): the same order of the top 50 probes and a relative 1e-8 on mean, log2 fold change, t, df, p value and adjusted p value; counts of probes tested (12488) and at FDR 0.05 (29) exact; every number in the report bound to the results file (none unbound); the not-limma statement, the transformation and the unknown genome build present.

briefs.title: A series on two platforms: the platform is a choice, never a guess (GSE1456)
briefs.why: GSE1456 was run on GPL96 and GPL97, so it has no single series matrix. A run must meet that outcome by name, choose the platform the question needs with a stated reason, analyse one platform only, and never pool the two.

inputs.groupDefinition: Using the tumour annotations in the series, compare the two most different groups the annotations define on the platform you judge most suitable, and say why you chose it.

mustDo: Call gene_expression_series with only the accession first, receive multi_platform_series with the platform list, and call again with one platform.
State the platform chosen and the reason; analyse that platform only.
Declare disjoint groups of at least three samples from the annotations (by accession or by an exact annotation value) and report the identity checks, including what stays unknown.
mustNotDo: Guess a platform before the tool names the choices, merge samples of two platforms into one analysis, or treat probe identifiers of different platforms as the same.
Claim agreement with another study or a limma result.
briefs.gradedOn: The multi-platform outcome was met and resolved by an explicit platform argument; one platform in the results (series.platform); two disjoint groups with at least three samples each; identity checks reported with unknowns stated; numbers rendered, not typed; the report names what the tool does not adjust for (batch, pairing, covariates).

briefs.title: A series over the samples limit is refused for that computation, and the conversation continues (GSE4922)
briefs.why: A resource limit protects the deployment, not an opinion: the Uppsala breast cancer series is published as about 250 arrays on GPL96, which is more than the default 200-sample limit. The run must name the limit and carry on with what it can still do.

inputs.groupDefinition: Compare the highest and lowest tumour grade groups in this series.

mustDo: Call gene_expression_series with accession and platform. Where the deployment's samples limit is below the series' sample count the tool refuses with gene_expression_input_over_limit naming limit samples, the count and the limit; say that this computation was not done and why, and that no statistic was estimated by hand.

Offer what the researcher can still do (a smaller series, or a subset of the data brought in as a file for the ordinary statistical analysis), and write the short report that says so without inventing a result.
If the deployment's limit was raised above the series' size, run the normal flow of brief 001 instead and record that the limit was not met.
mustNotDo: Compute the comparison some other way to get around the refusal, or describe the refusal as the series being empty or missing.
Retry the same call unchanged as if the refusal were an outage.
briefs.gradedOn: The refusal named the limit (samples), the observed count and the allowed count; no results file was written; the delivered report states the computation was not done and why; the operator counter open_science_gene_expression_limits_total{limit="samples"} increased by one for the run (checked on the deployment); no number in the report that no tool produced.
